messages:
olivia_sales: Hey team — kickoff with Sandstone tomorrow. They want a Private deployment POC but netops is asking whether we should push PrivateLink+proxy or just VPC peering + NAT. Need quick list of tradeoffs, firewall rules, and any pricing delta to flag.

alex_netops: +1. Key tradeoffs: PrivateLink = endpoint in their VPC, no route table changes, easier for strict netsec; VPC peering = full L3, simpler egress but might expose more surface area.

riya_se: For a POC I'd recommend PrivateLink if they require strict allowlists and minimal routing changes. Also easier to preserve source IP with edge proxies if they need it.

matt_infra: Pricing: PrivateLink has data-processing hit on our side and per-GB transfer on AWS side for endpoint traffic. Peering mainly costs us cross-AZ traffic and requires NAT/EIP if they have internet egress rules. We should surface an estimated $/GB swing (roughly 0.5–2c/GB depending on region) — will confirm exact numbers.

olivia_sales: Good. Sandstone explicitly called out finance and security review — they asked for firewall port list (+ examples for FQDN allowlist). Can someone paste the minimal ports?

alex_netops: Minimal egress from customer to our edge: TCP 443 outbound to our service IP(s) or FQDN. If using PrivateLink, they'll create an interface endpoint and route to that — no public IPs needed. Sample allowlist:

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood endpoints
ALLOW TCP 443 to *.redwood-inference.com
ALLOW TCP 443 to 54.23.12.34  # example eip for edge proxy
```

riya_se: Also mention DNS: with PrivateLink they should configure the VPC endpoint DNS (or Route53 private hosted zone). If they use peering, ensure resolver rules to avoid split-horizon resolution issues.

sara_sales: Sandstone asked about preserving client source IP for logging. Which setup preserves it?

matt_infra: Short answer: If they go through our managed proxy in their VPC (PrivateLink + ENI), we can preserve src IP via X-Forwarded-For headers but the TCP source will be our ENI. If they self-proxy across peering and NAT, original src IP is preserved inside the VPC but may be SNATed on egress. We'll document both scenarios.

security_bot: Sandstone submitted the security questionnaire v2. Key asks: encryption in transit, key management, audit logs, and network segmentation. We should attach a one-pager covering: TLS certs (TLS1.2+), optional KMS for private deploy, VPC flow logs + SIEM integration, and support for private control plane.

olivia_sales: Can someone draft a concise answer for the questionnaire items around "network connectivity and firewall rules"? We need it by EOD to push to procurement.

alex_netops: Draft below — feel free to edit before I send: 

"Redwood supports Private deployments via interface endpoints (PrivateLink) or VPC peering. For PrivateLink, customers create an interface endpoint in their VPC; outbound firewall rules only need to allow TCP/443 to our service FQDNs. DNS can be routed to our private hosted zone. For VPC peering, route tables must be updated and customers should allow TCP/443 to our peering CIDR; NAT/EIP may be required for internet-bound requests. VPC Flow Logs and mutual TLS are supported; logging and audit events can be exported to customer S3 or SIEM via our log-forwarding integrations."

riya_se: LGTM. I'll add the bit about recommended security posture: (1) PrivateLink for regulated workloads, (2) peering for low-latency internal-only use, (3) use AWS Private CA or KMS if they need customer-managed keys.

olivia_sales: Perfect. Matt — can you confirm the rough cost delta so I can give procurement a ballpark?

matt_infra: I'll pull region numbers and post by 16:30 PST. For now tell them 1) PrivateLink may incur per-hour endpoint fees + per-GB data charges on AWS, 2) Peering shifts cost to their NAT/EIP and cross-AZ. Estimate: PrivateLink ~ +$0.01–0.03/GB vs peering in most regions.

sara_sales: Thanks — I'll incorporate those into the POC statement of work and send Sandstone a one-page connectivity appendix. :thumbsup:

olivia_sales: Awesome. If anyone sees a blocker (esp legal/SOC items) call it out now. Otherwise I'll send draft and questionnaire answers to Sandstone this afternoon. :rocket:
